title: Commitment Approval Queue and Legal Handshake — Cross-functional SOP
author: Daniela Martinez
content:
Overview:
This document defines the operational flow, responsibilities, SLAs, and handoff artifacts for purchase commitments that require legal contract review and create revenue recognition/billing implications. It is intended for Finance, Legal, Procurement, Sales/Account Management, and Engineering teams who originate or manage commercial commitments.

Scope:
- Covers commitments that create a contractual obligation (subscription, reserved/dedicated capacity, multi-year commitments, SOWs, and enterprise support contracts).
- Excludes purely internal purchase orders (hardware/software purchases with no customer contract).

Goals:
- Ensure commitments are approved and recorded in forecasts within defined timelines.
- Standardize the legal handoff so contract language does not delay billing or revrec.
- Define a clear queue/triage and escalation path for approvals and exceptions.

Key Definitions:
- Commitment: Any customer or partner agreement creating a multi-period obligation or payment schedule (subscription, reserved capacity, committed spend).
- Revenue Trigger: The point at which Finance is authorized to record deferred revenue and/or issue invoices.
- Legal Handoff: The formal transfer of contract artifacts (redlines, signature pages, SOWs) from Legal to Finance/Revenue Ops and Procurement.

Approval Matrix (thresholds and approvers):
| Commitment Value (ARR equivalent) | Required Approvals | Primary Approver SLA | Notes |
|----------------------------------|--------------------|---------------------|-------|
| <= $50,000                       | Deal Owner + Finance | 3 business days     | Standard billing terms template OK |
| $50,001 - $250,000               | Deal Owner + Finance + Legal | 5 business days | Legal review required for non-standard clauses |
| $250,001 - $1,000,000            | Deal Owner + Finance + Legal + Sales Director | 7 business days | May require procurement/PO coordination for customers with procurement constraints |
| > $1,000,000                     | Deal Owner + CFO + GC + Sales VP | 10 business days | Executive notification; procurement may require additional KYC/credit checks |

Required Artifacts for Legal Handoff (attach to the approval ticket):
- Fully executed contract or final redline PDF (signed pages if available)
- Statement of Work (SOW) or Order Form with line-item billing cadence
- Pricing worksheets and discount approvals (signed pricing attestation)
- Customer billing/legal contact and invoicing address (including billing email and PO requirements)
- Implementation acceptance criteria (if recognized on delivery/milestones)
- Any compliance or data residency attachments (if applicable)

Operational Workflow (numbered procedure):
1. Origin: Sales/Account Manager creates an approval ticket in the procurement/commitments queue (JIRA ticket type: COMMITMENT-REQ) using the template below.
2. Finance Triage (within 2 business days): Finance validates that the commitment is reflected in the latest forecast bucket and assigns a forecast owner. If the commitment is material to forecast variance (>5% of ARR bucket), Finance flags for Forecast Committee review.
3. Legal Review (standard SLA: 5 business days): Legal triages for non-standard clauses (IP, indemnity caps, data residency, escrow, KMS). Legal provides either: approved contract, commentary with required edits, or escalates to GC for >$1M deals.
4. Procurement/PO Coordination (if customer requires PO): Procurement issues internal PO or confirms external PO flow to Accounts Receivable.
5. Signature & Artifact Collection: Once signed, Sales uploads the executed contract and the signature page into the ticket and moves the ticket to the "Handoff to Revenue Ops" status.
6. Revenue Ops/Billing (within 3 business days of handoff): Revenue Ops validates recognition model (subscription vs. milestone), assigns revenue recognition code, and creates the billing schedule in the billing system (NetSuite/Stripe/Zuora integration).
7. Forecast Update & Recognition Trigger: Finance updates MRR/ARR forecasts and, if recognition criteria are met, records a deferred revenue schedule. Any exceptions (e.g., acceptance criteria not met) are noted and posted to the contract record.
8. Post-Mortem: For any deal that misses SLAs or causes >10% forecast variance, the cross-functional team runs a 10-day incident review.

JIRA Ticket Template (COMMITMENT-REQ):
- Summary: [Customer] - [Product/Capacity] - [Currency Amount] - [Contract Type]
- Fields: Customer legal name; Sales Owner; Deal Value (ARR/EAC); Renewal/Start/End Date; Billing cadence; Required PO? Y/N; Attachments: draft contract, pricing sheet, SOW.
- Workflow statuses: New -> Finance Triage -> Legal Review -> Procurement (if PO) -> Handoff to Revenue Ops -> Billing Scheduled -> Closed

Legal Review Prioritization Rules:
- Expedited (48 hours): Security incident remediation agreements, legal holds, and customers requiring urgent cutoff dates.
- Standard (5 business days): Most SaaS/reserved capacity agreements using approved templates.
- Extended (10 business days): Complex multi-party agreements, export controls, or material IP transfers.

Escalation Path:
1. If Legal review exceeds SLA, Legal lead notifies Sales leader and Finance lead within 24 hours after SLA breach.
2. If procurement PO is delayed >7 business days, Procurement lead notifies Sales Ops and the customer procurement contact.
3. For high-value deals (> $1M) in active exception, the GC + CFO schedule a 1:1 review within 48 hours of escalation.

Revenue Recognition Checklist for Revenue Ops (required for RevRec posting):
- Contract type confirmed: Subscription / Usage / Milestone / One-time.
- Billing cadence: Monthly / Quarterly / Annual / Milestone-based.
- Start date for recognition: Signed date / Service start / Acceptance sign-off.
- Performance obligations explicitly listed in contract and mapped to revenue schedule.
- External customer PO or billing requirements documented.
- Any customer acceptance criteria or holdbacks captured with expected dates.
- GL codes and deferred revenue accounts assigned.

Sample Approval Matrix Table (CSV-friendly):
threshold,approvers,legal_sla,finance_sla,notes
50000,Sales Owner;Finance,3bd,2bd,standard template ok
250000,Sales Owner;Finance;Legal,5bd,2bd,legal review required
1000000,Sales Owner;CFO;GC;Sales VP,10bd,3bd,exec review

Common Exceptions and How to Handle Them:
- Customer requires campus/department-specific PO: Procurement to create a PO template and confirm split-invoicing if required.
- Data residency clauses or KMS requirements: Flag to Security & Compliance and Legal; include expected 10 business day review window.
- Discounting beyond approved threshold: Sales must attach Pricing Exception Approval signed by Revenue Operations + Finance.

Operational Metrics and Reporting:
- KPI 1: % of commitments processed within SLA (target: 95%).
- KPI 2: Average Legal review time (target: <= 4 business days for standard deals).
- KPI 3: Time from signature to first invoice (target: <= 5 business days).
- KPI 4: Number of forecast adjustments attributable to post-signature changes (target: < 3% monthly).

Roles & Responsibilities (short list):
- Sales/Deal Owner: Initiate ticket, attach artifacts, drive customer signature.
- Legal: Provide contract review, flag non-standard terms, sign-off on final language.
- Finance: Triage commitments, update forecasts, own revrec treatment.
- Procurement: Ensure PO flow, vendor/customer procurement onboarding if required.
- Revenue Ops/Billing: Create billing schedules, issue invoices, maintain recognition schedules.

Backout / Remediation Steps (if a signed contract cannot be recognized immediately):
1. Tag contract as "Pending Acceptance" in the system with reason code (e.g., implementation dependency).
2. Finance records a note and defers recognition; Revenue Ops schedules first invoice to be blocked until acceptance.
3. Account Manager to provide weekly status updates until acceptance criteria are met.
4. If outstanding beyond 90 days, escalate to Sales Director and Finance for resolution; consider credit memo or amendment.

Appendix A — Example Clause Language to Avoid (Legal Notes):
- Open-ended indemnities or unlimited liability without caps.
- Ambiguous acceptance criteria that delay start date determination.
- Auto-renewal terms without clear notice periods (Finance needs clear renewal triggers for forecasting).

Appendix B — Quick Contact Roster:

- Revenue Ops: revenue-ops@redwood.ai
- Legal Intake: legal-intake@redwood.ai

Notes for implementers:
- Use the COMMITMENT-REQ ticket exactly; missing attachments are the leading cause of SLA misses.
- Maintain an automated dashboard (Looker/Metabase) showing ticket age by stage; Finance and Legal leads must review weekly.
